Content.Primitive: Messrs. IV. Black wood 6l Sons have a list of books which one and all invite attention. Possibly the most interesting item of news is the announcement of a new and enlarged edition of Stephens' 'Book of the Farm,' the new editor being Mr. James Macdonald, of the Farming World, who has had the benefit of the _assistance of some of the best agricultural authorities of the day. The publishers in their preliminary announcement hope that this, the fourth edition of ' The Book of the Farm,' in its greatly extended and thoroughly revised form, may efficiently help the farmer to pursue his occupation with pleasure and profit. Farming, if it is to continue to maintain its importance as an industry, must, like any other business, be conducted at a profit. With reduced prices and other magnified obstacles it is more difficult than ever to accomplish this. More than ever, therefore, it is important that the farmer should fortify himself with all the guidance, stimulus, and encouragement which * The Book of the Farm' is capable of affording to him. The work is designed as a guide to him in every piece of practical work and every item of farming business he is called upon to engage in. It presents itself as a faithful compendium of the experience of a whole army of agricultural ' specialists,' and thus forms in itself a comprehensive professional library for every wellequipped farmer.
